accepted.question_text: Let n >= 2 and let S be a submodule of the Hardy space H^2(D^n). For each coordinate z_j, let R_zj be multiplication by z_j restricted to S, and let E_zj be the compression to S of evaluation at zero in the z_j variable. Given a subset Lambda of {1,...,n}, characterize exactly when S can be represented as a closed sum S = sum_{i in Lambda} phi_i(z_i) H^2(D^n), where each phi_i is an inner function of the single variable z_i. Is this representation equivalent to the defect equations (I_S - E_zl E_zl*)(I_S - R_zl R_zl*) = 0 for l outside Lambda and (I_S - E_zi E_zi*)(I_S - R_zi R_zi*)(I_S - E_zj E_zj*)(I_S - R_zj R_zj*) = 0 for all distinct i,j in Lambda?

Let Lambda and Gamma be subsets of {1,...,n}. For inner functions phi_j and psi_j of one complex variable, define submodules S_{Phi_Lambda} = sum_{lambda in Lambda} phi_lambda(z_lambda) H^2(D^n) and S_{Psi_Gamma} = sum_{t in Gamma} psi_t(z_t) H^2(D^n). Characterize when the orthogonal projections P_{S_{Phi_Lambda}} and P_{S_{Psi_Gamma}} commute. In particular, is commutativity equivalent to the divisibility alternative that, for every j in Lambda intersect Gamma, either phi_j divides psi_j or psi_j divides phi_j?
accepted.context_brief: Commuting projections for sums of inner submodules

evidence.quote: [P_{\mathcal{S}_{\Phi_{\Lambda}}},P_{\mathcal{S}_{\Psi_{\Gamma}}}]=0 if and only if either \varphi_{j}|\psi_{j} or \psi_{j}|\varphi_{j}

accepted.question_text: Let S be a submodule of H^2(D^n). For each coordinate z_i, let z_i S be the image of S under coordinate multiplication, and let S minus z_i S denote the orthogonal complement of z_i S inside S. Characterize when S minus z_i S is orthogonal to S minus z_j S for every distinct pair i,j in {1,...,n}; equivalently, characterize when the coordinate restriction defect projections satisfy (I_S - R_zi R_zi*)(I_S - R_zj R_zj*) = 0 for every distinct i,j.

evidence.quote: when does the condition \mathcal{S}\ominus z_{i}\mathcal{S}\perp\mathcal{S}\ominus z_{j}\mathcal{S} holds for all distinct i,j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}?
